title: pastinaca glacialis
intro: Pastinaca glacialis, commonly known as Wild Parsnip, is a biennial herb plant native to Europe and Asia, characterized by its hollow, ribbed stems and umbrella-like clusters of white or yellowish flowers. The plant has been used in traditional medicine for its numerous health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which can aid in reducing inflammation, improving immune function, and protecting against oxidative stress. The therapeutic actions of Wild Parsnip include stimulating digestion, reducing fever, and alleviating respiratory issues such as coughs and colds. The bioactive constituents of the plant include sesquiterpenes, alkaloids, and flavonoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and have been shown to have antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory effects.
